elements.element: Customer is not subject to any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 continues to prohibit the Company from participating in any Internet project similar to the Site with respect to Deerskin Products.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 continues to grant HDI the exclusive right to use the Deerskin brand for a self-contained direct-to-consumer website, restricting the Company's use in that field.

elements.element: The restriction is limited to a named competing product.
elements.evidence: The restriction is limited to the capitalized Deerskin Products; the broader references to substantially similar products and other companies have been removed.

elements.element: The restriction applies only during the term of the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 expressly applies “during the term of this Agreement,” and the added sentence confirms that the restriction applies during the term.

elements.element: The restriction is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states that the restriction applies “in any event for no longer than 12 months.”

elements.element: The restriction includes a carve-out for internal development.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states that the restriction shall not prevent the Company from internally developing web sites.

elements.element: The restriction includes a carve-out for acquisitions.
elements.evidence: The added sentence permits the Company to continue operating any business or web site acquired by the Company.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because operative non-compete and field-of-use exclusivity restrictions remain. It does achieve every fallback element by narrowing the covered products, limiting the restriction to the term and no more than 12 months, and adding internal-development and acquisition carve-outs. The changes are targeted and preserve the remaining exclusivity framework, although the duration sentence redundantly repeats the term limitation and could state the 12-month measurement point more precisely.
